descriptionChirho: The head or poll as a unit for counting individuals in a census or assessment. Hebrew gulgōlet in this sense functions as a distributive measure meaning 'per head' or 'per capita,' used in census-taking contexts in Numbers 1 (tribal military enrollment) and 1 Chronicles 23 (Levitical census), as well as Exodus 16:16 and 38:26 for the per-person measure of manna and the half-shekel census tax. The plural with possessive suffix (legulgolotām 'by their polls') is the standard census formula.

The bony structure of the head, the cranium or skull in its literal anatomical sense. Used in Judges 9:53 where a woman drops a millstone on Abimelech's skull (gulgaltō), in 2 Kings 9:35 where only Jezebel's skull, feet, and palms remain after being consumed by dogs, and in 1 Chronicles 10:10 where the Philistines fasten Saul's skull in the temple of Dagon. All occurrences involve violent death and the physical remains of the cranium.
